record.context_brief: Fixed points of the parts-multiplicities involution
record.original_question: Let T(n) be the set of partitions of n in which all nonzero multiplicities are distinct, and let sigma_n be the involution on T(n) obtained by interchanging the list of parts with the list of multiplicities and then reordering so that the multiplicities are increasing. Determine the asymptotic number of fixed points of sigma_n.

evidence.quote: Wilf (2010) mentions a mapping on T(n) in which the roles of parts and multiplicities are interchanged. We let sigma_n denote this mapping.
It is an open problem to find (asymptotics for) the number of fixed points of sigma_n.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a positive integer $n$, let $T(n)$ denote the set of partitions of $n$ with the property that all nonzero multiplicities are distinct; that is, partitions in which no two distinct parts appear the same positive number of times. Given $\lambda \in T(n)$ with distinct parts $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_k$ occurring with multiplicities $m_1, m_2, \ldots, m_k$ (which are pairwise distinct positive integers), define an involution $\sigma_n : T(n) \to T(n)$ as follows: let $b_1 < b_2 < \cdots < b_k$ be the multiplicities $m_1, \ldots, m_k$ rearranged in increasing order, and let $\pi$ be the permutation such that $b_i = m_{\pi(i)}$; then $\sigma_n(\lambda)$ is the partition whose distinct parts are $b_1 < \cdots < b_k$ with the part $b_i$ occurring with multiplicity $a_{\pi(i)}$. (Equivalently, $\sigma_n$ interchanges the lists of parts and multiplicities and reorders so that the new multiplicities are increasing.) Let $F(n)$ denote the number of fixed points of $\sigma_n$. Determine the asymptotic behavior of $F(n)$ as $n \to \infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved. Subsequent work (in particular a paper titled "The Number of Fixed Points of Wilf's Partition Involution," arXiv:1307.6391, published in the Electronic Journal of Combinatorics, 2013) established an asymptotic formula, including the relation log F(n) ~ (1/2) log f(n), where f(n) counts all partitions of n with distinct multiplicities.

status_evidence.title: The number of fixed points of Wilf's partition involution
status_evidence.snippet: Determines an asymptotic formula for the number F(n) of fixed points of Wilf's partition involution.
status_evidence.claim: The asymptotic count of fixed points of the involution σ_n was determined.

status_evidence.title: The Number of Fixed Points of Wilf's Partition Involution - Electronic Journal of Combinatorics
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic formula log F(n) ~ (1/2) log f(n) is obtained.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotics for the number of fixed points were established.
